conceptNote: A device is a named, reusable unit of dramatic expression that is (a) expressible in the storyboard schema, (b) has a stated intent, and (c) has a stated failure mode from overuse. A technique with no 'avoidWhen' becomes a tic. A technique the schema cannot express is a wish, not a device.

devices.name: Two-panel exchange
devices.intent: Show both participants of an exchange so reaction and statement read together. The workhorse layout for two-person dialogue.
devices.useWhen: Two characters are in conversation and the listener's reaction carries meaning.
devices.avoidWhen: The line is a revelation or a punchline that should own the whole frame, or the listener has nothing to express.
devices.schemaExpression: layout=split2 with two character panels; speaker's panel expression suitableFor speaking, listener's suitableFor listening.
devices.budget: Default layout. Should be the majority of dialogue scenes but not all of them.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: 'use split-screen more frequently, especially during the Anton–Veronika dialogue'.

devices.name: Solo full-frame emphasis
devices.intent: Give one character the entire frame so the line lands without competition.
devices.useWhen: Opening line of a sequence, a revelation, a punchline, or a reply that must feel isolated.
devices.avoidWhen: The other character's reaction is the point of the beat.
devices.schemaExpression: layout=single with one character panel, shot=medium.

devices.name: Close-up on a turning point
devices.intent: Increase intensity by cropping tighter, marking the line as more important than its neighbours.
devices.useWhen: Disbelief, realisation, sudden excitement, or a final wordless reaction.
devices.avoidWhen: Ordinary conversational lines, explanations, or two consecutive scenes in a row.
devices.budget: At most ~1 in 5 scenes. Two consecutive close-ups are a defect unless the second is a silent reaction.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: 'avoiding constant close-ups; reserving close-ups for disbelief, realization, excitement, or a final reaction'.

devices.name: Extreme close-up
devices.intent: Maximum intensity: eyes and brow fill the frame.
devices.useWhen: Once per video at most, on the single strongest emotional peak.
devices.avoidWhen: Anywhere else. It has no gradation left above it.
devices.budget: Maximum one per project. Requires source asset ≥2048px or it will visibly soften.
devices.evidence: GTA:SA key art (wide-eyed panel); unused in zayavka-v1.

devices.name: All-cast reaction split
devices.intent: Show every character reacting to the same statement simultaneously.
devices.useWhen: One line lands on the whole group: an announcement, an absurdity, a shared realisation.
devices.avoidWhen: Cast of one or two. With two characters this is just DEV-SPLIT-DIALOGUE.
devices.schemaExpression: layout=split3 with three character panels, all listener-suitable expressions, and either a silent beat or one short line.
devices.budget: At most once or twice per project; it resolves nothing and stops the conversation.

devices.name: Delayed second-character reveal
devices.intent: Open on one character alone, then widen to a split when the second character answers, so their arrival is an event.
devices.useWhen: First exchange of a conversation, or a new character entering the scene.
devices.avoidWhen: Mid-conversation, where it reads as an arbitrary layout change.
devices.schemaExpression: Scene N: layout=single with character A. Scene N+1: layout=split2 with A and B, B speaking.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: 'beginning the main dialogue with Anton alone, then revealing Veronika when she answers'.

devices.name: Detail or gesture insert
devices.intent: Replace a face panel with a hand, a fist, or an object to carry subtext the face cannot.
devices.useWhen: Tension, threat, dismissal, or a physical beat: closed fists, a pointing hand, a dismissive wave.
devices.avoidWhen: The emotion is already legible on the face; the insert then just hides information.
devices.schemaExpression: A panel with kind=insert and its own asset, in either a single or split layout.
devices.budget: Requires a dedicated generated asset outside the expression sheet. Budget one per project in MVP.
devices.evidence: GTA:CTW cutscene at 27.8s replaces the second character's panel with a pointing-hand panel.

devices.name: Sustained portrait hold
devices.intent: Keep one unchanged image across several consecutive lines and let the text carry the performance.
devices.useWhen: A character delivers two or more connected sentences; a long explanation; any moment where changing the image would add nothing.
devices.avoidWhen: The character's emotion genuinely shifts mid-speech.
devices.schemaExpression: One dialogue scene containing multiple lines, or consecutive scenes with identical panels.
devices.budget: Not merely permitted but encouraged. The reference cutscene holds one static portrait for ~12 seconds across two sentences.
devices.evidence: GTA:CTW cutscene 12.4s–24.2s holds a single portrait across two full sentences.

devices.name: Silent reaction beat
devices.intent: A scene with no text at all, so the audience watches a face instead of reading.
devices.useWhen: Immediately after a punchline, an insult, or a revelation. Mandatory after a punchline.
devices.avoidWhen: Before the audience has been given anything to react to.
devices.schemaExpression: A dialogue scene whose single line has text="", beat=silentReaction, revealFrames=0.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: 'without that reaction, the punchline did not fully land'.

devices.name: List-of-three escalation
devices.intent: Split an enumeration into separate short lines with shortening or lengthening holds to build comic rhythm.
devices.useWhen: The script contains a list, especially one whose third item is the joke.
devices.avoidWhen: The items are not parallel in structure, or there are more than four.
devices.schemaExpression: One scene, several short lines with beat=listItem, and the final item given a longer hold and an ellipsis.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: one continuous line rewritten into three beats with a pause before the third.

devices.name: Split thought with a pause
devices.intent: Break one utterance into two lines so the pause between them carries meaning.
devices.useWhen: A character concedes something and then asks a question; a realisation followed by its consequence.
devices.avoidWhen: The two halves are not separable thoughts; you get stutter, not rhythm.
devices.schemaExpression: Two lines in the same scene, first with beat=acknowledgement or quickBeat.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: 'Interesting approach. How can this be interesting?' became 'An unusual approach.' + pause + 'Why would people want to use it?'.

devices.name: Fullscreen text interstitial
devices.intent: Skip time or change location for free, with no image cost at all.
devices.useWhen: A time jump ('Несколько мгновений позже'), a chapter break, or a deliberate rhythm stop.
devices.avoidWhen: More than twice per project, or to paper over a story gap the script should have handled.
devices.budget: Zero asset cost. The cheapest device in the catalog.

devices.name: Closing text card
devices.intent: End on a written joke or mock disclaimer rather than trailing off on a face.
devices.useWhen: The story has landed and a written coda extends the joke.
devices.avoidWhen: There is no joke to extend; a silent reaction beat is the better ending.
devices.evidence: owner request, 2026-09-17: 'no ... were harmed when producing this video'.

devices.name: Cast title strip
devices.intent: Introduce each character by name and role before the dialogue starts, so the audience does not have to infer who is who.
devices.useWhen: Cast of two or three whose identity or job matters to the joke.
devices.avoidWhen: Videos under ~40 seconds, where 3–4 seconds per character is too much of the runtime.
devices.schemaExpression: kind=template, templateId=cast-panel-strip, one slot per character.
devices.budget: Requires one title-framed portrait per character at a DIFFERENT framing from the dialogue portraits. This is an extra generated asset per character, not free reuse.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 IntroSequences.tsx; GTA:SA angled-panel key art.

devices.name: Contextual opening shot
devices.intent: Establish the situation in one image before anyone speaks.
devices.useWhen: The premise needs a frame of reference the dialogue would otherwise waste lines explaining.
devices.avoidWhen: The premise is self-evident from the first exchange.
devices.schemaExpression: kind=template with a context template, or a dialogue scene with a single insert panel and no lines.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 ApplicationPOV; GTA:CTW establishing medium shot at 0.6s.

devices.name: Mirror for gaze convergence
devices.intent: Flip a panel so two characters in a split layout look toward each other instead of both looking the same way.
devices.useWhen: In split2, both characters' gaze or head orientation point the same direction.
devices.avoidWhen: The asset is not flipSafe, or the drift is in facial proportion rather than direction — mirroring cannot fix an off-model face.
devices.schemaExpression: panel.flipHorizontal=true, permitted only when the expression entry has flipSafe=true.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1: Veronika's 'active explanation' looked the wrong way; flipping would have fixed the gaze but not the facial drift, so the asset was regenerated instead.

devices.name: Expression change on speech onset
devices.intent: Change only the incoming speaker's expression when they begin talking, leaving the listener untouched.
devices.useWhen: Every speaker change. This is the default, not a flourish.
devices.avoidWhen: Never avoided; but it must not be accompanied by a simultaneous listener change unless deliberateReaction is set with a reason.
devices.schemaExpression: Between adjacent scenes, exactly one panel's expressionId changes.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 owner correction: Veronika acquiring a raised-finger gesture at the start of Anton's line, then holding it while listening.

devices.name: Slow push-in
devices.intent: Remove the dead-static feel of a held image with a very slow scale ramp.
devices.useWhen: Deferred for v1. When enabled it is a style-preset constant applied to all single-panel shots, NOT a per-scene directorial choice.
devices.avoidWhen: Any per-scene or directional use, until the Director has a track record on the simpler devices.
devices.schemaExpression: style.kenBurnsScale > 1.0. There is deliberately no per-scene field.
devices.budget: Requires source assets ≥2048px or the push-in will visibly soften the image.
devices.evidence: zayavka-v1 IntroSequences.tsx already does this at 1.08→1.0 and 1.045→1.0.
